summary.headline: Kranti Industries FY26 consolidated revenue crossed ₹100 crore for the first time; standalone PAT turned to ₹260 lakh from a ₹75 lakh loss.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as transformational: consolidated revenue crossed ₹100 crore for the first time, standalone revenue rose 30% to ₹93.88 crore, and standalone EBITDA margin expanded from 10.5% to 13.3%. Q4 FY26 standalone revenue of ₹29.31 crore was the company's highest quarterly figure, up 60.2% YoY and 28.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of ₹167 lakh, which management attributed to start-up costs of the new Jaipur plant. The company entered defence machining (orders from AVNL) and commissioned its fourth facility in Jaipur from January 1, 2026, which it took on lease along with an acquired operation.

financial_highlights.value: Crossed ₹100 crore (first time in company history)

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of ₹75 lakh in FY25
vs loss of ₹308 lakh in FY25

segments.name: Agriculture / tractors
segments.commentary: Management confirmed tractors are the major revenue source; the company was almost 95% agriculture-dependent five years ago at about ₹20 crore revenue. Diversification now stands at around 16%.

segments.name: Electric vehicles
segments.commentary: EV components contributed about 5.3% of FY26 revenue across Kalyani Techno Forge (one passenger-car EV component, one production line running for 12-15 months), Dana group and Eka Mobility.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Entered defence through machining orders from AVNL; management targets PSU tenders directly rather than Tier-2/Tier-3 supply, and expects 4-6 more quarters to build a substantial position.

segments.name: Jaipur plant (Plant-4)
segments.commentary: Commercial operations began January 1, 2026 with over 35,000 sq ft of machining capacity; utilisation was below 40% in the first quarter, and FY27 revenue is guided at ₹12-14 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 Jaipur (Plant-4) revenue expected at ₹12-14 crore.
Management expects double-digit YoY growth from here, barring extraordinary events.
EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at 18-20% at about 85% utilisation with a better product mix, most likely by FY28 rather than FY27.
Priorities for FY27: ramp up Jaipur utilisation, improve efficiency, expand exports, deepen defence, industrial, construction equipment and EV presence, and improve working capital efficiency.
Further acquisitions are not planned immediately, but remain on the Vision 2030 roadmap for both organic and inorganic growth.
capex_capacity: Fourth facility in Jaipur, Rajasthan, commissioned with commercial operations from January 1, 2026; adds over 35,000 sq ft of machining capacity. Plant, machinery and business were taken on lease with an exclusive 100% machining arrangement with one customer.
Pune facility utilisation is about 65%; management sees the practical maximum at 80-85%.
Continuing investment in CNC machining infrastructure, automation, process improvements and quality systems.
Q4 FY26 margin dilution attributed to short-term costs of capacity creation, which management expects to yield operating leverage as utilisation rises.
demand_pricing: Agriculture: management sees steady domestic tractor growth over three years and rising European and American agriculture demand.
Supply chain and inflation pressures from the ongoing war are being managed with customer support, per management; no specific impact quantified.
Defence: AVNL machining orders won; multiple customer visits, audits and executions in the last 14-18 months; the entry is slow because of PSU tendering processes.
China Plus One and localisation trends are cited as export and customer-diversification drivers; the company is also aiming to increase wallet share per customer.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Kalyani Techno Forge and EV revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: One EV passenger-car component has been supplied to KTFL for 12-15 months on one running line, with future volumes under discussion. EV components were about 5.3% of FY26 revenue, covering KTFL, Dana group and Eka Mobility.

qa_highlights.question: Any distress in rural demand, and war-related supply impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no rural distress. Domestic tractor demand has grown for three years and export agriculture demand is rising. Supply chain and inflation challenges exist, handled with customer support.

qa_highlights.question: Pune capacity utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Pune is at about 65% utilisation, with a practical maximum of 80-85%.

qa_highlights.question: Plant-4 utilisation and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation was below 40% in the first quarter of operation. FY27 revenue from Jaipur is expected at ₹12-14 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy for diversification and defence scaling?
qa_highlights.answer: The company targets direct PSU defence work rather than Tier-2/3 supply. Penetration will take another 4-6 quarters. Diversification is set to rise through defence, industrial engineering and higher wallet share per customer.

qa_highlights.question: Path to EBITDA margins?
qa_highlights.answer: At about 85% utilisation and with higher-margin parts, EBITDA margin is expected to stabilise at 18-20%, most likely by FY28.

risks_watch: Jaipur ramp-up: FY27 revenue of ₹12-14 crore depends on utilisation rising from below 40% at start.
Defence orders depend on PSU tendering timelines, with management expecting 4-6 quarters to build a substantial position.
Concentration: tractors remain the main revenue source, and Jaipur output is tied to one exclusive customer.
Supply chain and input cost inflation linked to the war, which management did not quantify.
Q4 EBITDA of ₹167 lakh on ₹29.31 crore revenue (about 5.7%) versus the FY26 margin of 13.3%; margin recovery needs to be tracked.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the long-term story and the 18-20% margin target, but cautious on near-term profitability. Management attributed the weak Q4 margin to start-up costs and was slow to commit on defence timing, saying it would take 4-6 quarters.
key_quotes: We expect double digit growth year on year from here because that is going to happen unless and until something extraordinary does not happen.
We believe these investments will generate meaningful operating leverage as utilization levels improve in the coming quarters.
So, we have an exclusive agreement where their business, 100% machining business will be routed through Kranti.

adds.what: Fourth facility in Jaipur (Plant-4), over 35,000 sq ft machining capacity, leased plant and business with exclusive 100% machining arrangement with one customer

growth.why: Management guides Jaipur Plant-4 FY27 revenue of ₹12-14 crore and double-digit YoY growth from here, backed by the commissioned Jaipur plant, a single-customer machining arrangement and AVNL defence orders, but no quantified order book or contract values were given and Jaipur utilisation was below 40%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides EBITDA margin to stabilise at 18-20% at about 85% utilisation, most likely by FY28, versus 13.3% FY26 standalone and only ~5.7% in Q4 FY26 due to Jaipur start-up costs.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Jaipur Plant-4 with over 35,000 sq ft machining capacity is already commercially operating; Pune is at about 65% utilisation with a practical max of 80-85%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Jaipur FY27 revenue guided at ₹12-14 crore and management expects double-digit YoY growth from here, against FY26 standalone revenue of ₹93.88 crore, though Jaipur utilisation was below 40% at start.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Pune utilisation is about 65%, below the 80% threshold, so no immediate capex trigger; continued CNC, automation and quality investment is noted but no new plant amount was guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is new and set conservatively as double-digit growth; Q4 margin was weak at about 5.7% and Jaipur ramp is unproven, so no upgrade signal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Jaipur must lift utilisation from below 40% to deliver ₹12-14 crore in FY27, and defence needs 4-6 quarters, with war-linked input inflation not quantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is deepening defence (AVNL machining orders), industrial and construction equipment and EV presence, but no specific new product launch date was given.

rows.label: Defence PSU machining ramp (AVNL)
rows.why: AVNL machining orders won and management expects 4-6 more quarters to build a substantial PSU defence position, though tendering timelines are slow.

rows.label: Single-customer exclusivity at Jaipur
rows.why: Jaipur plant runs an exclusive 100% machining arrangement with one customer, so ramp depends on that one customer's volumes, and no order value was disclosed.

rows.label: Export expansion and China Plus One
rows.why: Export expansion is a stated FY27 priority, citing China Plus One and rising European and American agriculture demand, but no export share or order number was quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on the long-term 18-20% margin target and the Jaipur plant, but cautious on near-term profitability and defence timing (4-6 quarters); analysts pressed on Jaipur utilisation (below 40%) and the EV and Pune headroom.

oneOffs.what: Jaipur Plant-4 taken on lease along with an acquired operation from January 1, 2026; the brief does not quantify its revenue contribution to Q4 or FY26 growth

quality.why: Standalone revenue grew 60.2% YoY in Q4 (₹29.31 crore) and 30% for FY26 (₹93.88 crore), but the brief does not say whether volume, price or mix drove it, and it gives no quantified one-off item; the new Jaipur plant and acquired operation may add inorganic revenue, though its size is not stated.
